title: Localization and Transport in a Non-Hermitian Hexagonal Harper Model
authors: Akshey Rajoriya, Dibyajyoti Sahu, Suhas Gangadharaiah, Tanay Nag
abstract: We investigate a one-dimensional non-Hermitian hexagonal Harper model with quasiperiodically modulated hopping amplitudes. In the Hermitian limit, the model exhibits metallic, insulating, and multifractal phases characterized by distinct eigenstate properties. Upon introducing non- Hermiticity, the phase diagram is qualitatively altered, with an expansion of metallic regions and strong boundary sensitivity arising from the non-Hermitian skin effect. By analyzing wave-packet dynamics, we uncover qualitatively distinct transport signatures in metallic, multifractal, and in- sulating regimes. In the metallic region, nonreciprocal hopping induces finite sliding, resulting in ballistic center-of-mass motion that is absent in the Hermitian model, while wave-packet spreading is simultaneously suppressed and exhibits diffusive scaling. Interestingly, the multifractal regime emerges as a distinct dynamical phase supporting both enhanced spreading and finite sliding, both primarily of superdiffusive nature, in contrast to metallic regions where sliding (spreading) shows ballistic (diffusive) scaling. These features are markedly different from their Hermitian counterpart. On the other hand, in the insulating region, both the spreading and sliding are strongly suppressed. We reconfirm these intriguing transport characteristics by investigating the distinct growth profile of single-particle entanglement entropy where the effect of spreading of the wave-packet is clearly manifested. These results demonstrate that quasiperiodicity in hopping amplitudes, combined with non-Hermiticity, establishes the multifractal regime as a key mediator of transport.
summary: The paper analyzes transport in a non-Hermitian hexagonal Harper model featuring quasiperiodic hopping. It finds that introducing non-Hermiticity dramatically alters the system's phases, particularly highlighting a unique multifractal regime. This regime supports distinct superdiffusive dynamics for both wave-packet spreading and center-of-mass motion, which are fundamentally different from the purely ballistic or diffusive behaviors seen in other regimes.
main_problem: The study investigates localization and transport properties within a one-dimensional non-Hermitian hexagonal Harper model subjected to quasiperiodically modulated hopping amplitudes.
main_result: Non-Hermiticity qualitatively alters the phase diagram, establishing the multifractal regime as a key mediator of transport characterized by superdiffusive dynamics, distinct from its Hermitian counterpart.
method: The analysis combines wave-packet dynamics to track center-of-mass motion and spreading, alongside spectral diagnostics like Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR) and entanglement entropy growth profiles.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D non-Hermitian hexagonal Harper model derived from an anisotropic lattice with quasiperiodic modulation ($\phi = (\sqrt{5}-1)/2$). The Hamiltonian incorporates hopping amplitudes modulated by the parameter $\eta$, which controls non-Hermiticity.
key_observables: Wave-packet spreading ($\sigma(t)$), center-of-mass motion (sliding velocity $v_s$), single-particle entanglement entropy growth, and localization measures like IPR and Fractal Dimension ($D_2$).
important_parameters: Non-Hermiticity strength ($\eta$), quasiperiodic flux ($\phi$), and the resulting phases: Metallic, Multifractal, and Insulating.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing results obtained under Periodic Boundary Conditions (PBC) versus Open Boundary Conditions (OBC), acknowledging the non-Hermitian skin effect in OBC calculations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the model's hopping structure; subsequent figures detail how wave-packet dynamics and localization measures change across different phases as $\eta$ is varied.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the non-Hermitian quasiperiodic model, then analyzing its phase diagram using spectral diagnostics (IPR/D2), followed by detailed dynamical studies of transport signatures (sliding vs. spreading) in each identified regime.
why_interesting: This work provides a rich theoretical framework for understanding how breaking time-reversal symmetry (non-Hermiticity) interacts with quasiperiodicity to fundamentally change quantum transport, offering insights applicable to open quantum systems and engineered lattices.
